description: Website frontend stability hardening PRD for the Vite + React workspace. Scope is the website frontend under frontend/ unless a story explicitly needs a mocked API contract. Do not include the WeChat mini program, backend worker behavior, production data repair, visual redesign, or new product features in this PRD.
globalRules: Read AGENTS.md and handoff.md before each story.
Work on exactly one user story per iteration.
Use the smallest possible frontend edit that satisfies the acceptance criteria.
Do not refactor unrelated code or rename files unless a story explicitly requires it.
Every completed story must include runnable proof through a temporary script.
A story can only be marked passes=true after frontend tests, frontend build, and git diff --check pass.
Commit each completed story separately after verification.

userStories.title: Create a single frontend stability proof runner
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need one documented local proof path for website frontend stability so future Ralph/Codex iterations do not guess which commands prove a frontend story.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a project-local frontend stability proof helper or documented command wrapper that runs npm --prefix frontend test, npm --prefix frontend run build, and git diff --check.
The helper must not depend on production data, secrets, or a running backend.
The helper output must make it obvious which command failed.
Run the helper from a temporary proof script and paste the full output.
Do not change business UI behavior in this story.
userStories.notes: This story creates the proof rail that all later stability stories reuse.

userStories.title: Harden website bootstrap and auth storage failures
userStories.description: As a user, I need the website to load without crashing even when browser storage is unavailable, stale, blocked, or partially cleared.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit App.tsx bootstrap token, organization, role, and workspace state reads for direct unsafe localStorage/sessionStorage access.
Add or extend tests so blocked storage and missing auth values do not crash initial render.
Unauthenticated users must land in the existing login/entry state, not a blank page.
No story work may introduce new direct window.localStorage.getItem reads outside the existing guarded helper pattern.
Run the frontend stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: Existing app-storage-guard coverage is the starting point.

userStories.title: Normalize frontend API failure states
userStories.description: As a teacher or admin, I need failed API calls to leave pages recoverable instead of stuck in loading, disabled, or stale partial states.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit shared apiFetch behavior and high-risk page-level catch blocks in App.tsx, SmartWrongQuestionsPage.tsx, CourseCalendarPage.tsx, and ClassFeedbackGenerationWorkspace.tsx.
Add focused tests for at least three representative failures: list load failure, save failure, and delete/refresh failure.
Each tested failure must clear loading/saving state and show the existing user-facing error path.
The fix must not change backend API contracts.
Run the frontend stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: Prefer existing alert/notice patterns; do not invent a new toast system.

userStories.title: Stabilize workspace navigation and permission fallbacks
userStories.description: As users with different roles, we need workspace navigation to hide inaccessible pages and recover cleanly when the current tab becomes unavailable.
acceptanceCriteria: Cover owner, admin, member, staff, and unauthenticated navigation paths with tests or existing source assertions.
If a selected workspace tab is not allowed for the current role, the UI must fall back to an allowed tab instead of rendering an empty or broken panel.
Navigation state must not preserve stale restricted pages after logout/login role changes.
Existing sidebar and dashboard copy should remain unchanged except where required for stability.
Run the frontend stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: Focus on website workspace navigation, not mini program routes.

userStories.title: Stabilize course calendar layout, filters, and drag/drop recovery
userStories.description: As a scheduler, I need the course calendar to stay usable when schedules, custom items, filters, or drag/drop operations fail or contain edge-case data.
acceptanceCriteria: Add tests for empty schedules, missing teacher/subject fields, long class names, and filtered classes with no matches.
Dropping a course or custom item must not leave the page in a pending-drop state if the API call fails or the user cancels adjustment.
Expanded calendar mode must keep the existing full-screen behavior without introducing nested page scroll traps.
Desktop and tablet layout assertions must keep the current independent scroll behavior for the right-side course/custom item lists.
Run the frontend stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: Existing course-calendar and course-calendar-data tests should be extended before UI changes.

userStories.title: Stabilize smart wrong question notebook and PDF actions
userStories.description: As a teacher, I need the smart wrong question notebook to remain recoverable when record loading, review saving, PDF refresh, delete, or practice generation fails.
acceptanceCriteria: Add focused tests for failed detail load, failed save, failed PDF refresh, failed delete, and failed practice-sheet generation.
A failed action must not close the notebook, lose unsaved editable fields, or leave buttons permanently disabled.
PDF preview and download links must consistently use the existing authenticated URL builder.
Deleting the selected record must keep the existing next-record or empty-detail behavior.
Run the frontend stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: This is a high-risk user workflow because it combines editing, PDF, and async actions.

userStories.title: Stabilize class feedback generation workspace actions
userStories.description: As a teacher, I need class feedback generation to handle loading, generating, saving, confirming, and member filtering edge cases without losing work.
acceptanceCriteria: Add tests for generate failure, save failure, confirm failure, and accessible-class/member selection changes.
Failed actions must clear busy state and preserve the current draft where the existing UI has editable content.
Changing accessible classes must not leave a selected class/member that is no longer available.
Existing workspace header/control bar placement must remain unchanged.
Run the frontend stability proof baseline.

userStories.title: Stabilize review and feedback async task polling
userStories.description: As a user waiting for generated output, I need async generation pages to recover from pending, failed, expired, or malformed task responses.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit review generation and class feedback polling paths for stuck pending states.
Add tests for pending response, failed response, malformed response, and retry/refresh behavior where the UI already supports it.
The UI must not show completed output until the response contains the required PDF or content fields.
Existing credit and backend semantics must not be changed from the frontend story.
Run the frontend stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: This story is frontend-only; backend worker reliability belongs in a separate backend PRD.

userStories.title: Stabilize class management and account administration forms
userStories.description: As an owner or admin, I need class management and account administration actions to prevent duplicate submission and recover after failed mutations.
acceptanceCriteria: Add tests or source assertions for disabled states on create, save, delete, refresh, invite, approval, and teacher-binding actions.
A failed mutation must release the relevant disabled state and keep the form data visible for correction.
Refreshing lists must not discard an expanded edit card unless the underlying record no longer exists.
No new backend endpoints may be added in this story.
Run the frontend stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: Existing account-card and class-management tests already assert several interaction locks.

userStories.title: Stabilize mobile and tablet scrolling behavior
userStories.description: As an iPad or mobile browser user, I need workspace pages to scroll naturally without sticky traps, horizontal overflow, or heavy visual effects during fast scrolling.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend mobile workspace performance tests to cover the main workspace shell and at least two high-risk pages with tall content.
The root shell must preserve the current native page scrolling and avoid body-level overscroll blocking.
No page should introduce a new full-screen nested scroll container beside the sidebar unless it is an intentional modal.
Heavy blur/filter effects must remain disabled or reduced on touch scrolling contexts where current CSS already guards them.
Run the frontend stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: This story protects recent iOS/iPad scroll fixes from regression.

userStories.title: Stabilize frontend math and PDF rendering inputs
userStories.description: As a teacher exporting materials, I need frontend KaTeX/PDF rendering to tolerate malformed math text and missing optional fields without blank or broken output.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend wrongQuestionLatex and render-wrong-question-library/practice-sheet tests for malformed escape sequences, bare LaTeX fragments, missing child reason, missing note, and geometry/image records.
Malformed math must degrade to readable text or existing render-failure UI; it must not crash React render or PDF markup generation.
PDF markup tests must verify non-empty question blocks for each covered record type.
Do not change backend PDF generation in this story.
Run the frontend stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: Keep this scoped to frontend render helpers and tests.

userStories.title: Add frontend stale-code and dead-path stability guardrails
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need obvious removed or deprecated frontend paths to stay removed so old UI branches do not silently reappear.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a lightweight frontend source guard test for deprecated website UI terms and dead paths already removed from the active product.
The guard must include only terms with clear current decisions recorded in handoff.md or existing tests.
Do not fail on historical docs, miniprogram files, or generated output.
The guard must be easy to extend when a future cleanup removes another path.
Run the frontend stability proof baseline.
userStories.notes: Examples from current handoff include removed old dashboard copy and hidden stale smart-wrong-question controls.
